1. Scope — Covers vegetable/chrome-tanned, stapled/lace-sewn small-size and large-size (ordinary 
as well as Bohemian) spring buffers used on over- pick looms. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — Shall be as given in Fig. 1 to 5. 

2.1 Positioning of Spindle Holes — The distance between the longitudinal axis of the loom spindle con- 
forming to IS : 7043-1973 'Specification for loom (fly) spindles' unless otherwise specified, inserted in 
the buffer and the plain surface at which the buffer would be resting shall be 17 to 19 mm when measured 
as shown in Fig. 1.

IS : 1737-1976 

3. Materials ~ Tanned-leather from buffalo or heavy ox hides. 

4. Workmanship 

4.1 The number of dry limed hide pieces to be introduced between the leather pieces shall not exceed 2 in 
any spring buffer. 

4.2 Each piece of leather as well as dry limed hide shall be without any splice or joint and there shall be no 
void discernible to naked eye, between the layers of the buffer, 

4.3 The position of the staples should be such that they do not touch the picker and remain as away as 
possible from the spindle hole. 

4.4 The nails used at pre-stapling stage should be removed after stapling. 

5. Fasteners 

5.1 Stitching — shall be with dry limed hide lacing 5 mm wide and 1 mm thick, using any suitable type of 
stitch. 

5.2 Stapling — shall be with 2 staples of mild steel or galvinized iron, wire 2-80 to 3-1 5 mm in diameter. 

6. Mass 

6.1 Sma// Size Spring Buffers — Zb±A, 92±5, or 99±5 g. 

6.2 Large Size Spring Buffers — 1 20±6, 1 28d=6, 1 35±7 or 1 42±7 g. 

7. Spindle Holes — Circular, corresponding to the particular spindle size given in IS : 7043-1 973 (unless 

-4-1 
otherwise specified) with a tolerance of _q mm on diameter. 

8. Packing — Shall be suitably packed as may be agreed to between the concerned parties. The package 
should contain fixed number of spring buffers essentially of the same variety. 

9. Marking — Each spring buffer shall bear the name of manufacturer or trade-mark, and a code number 
to trace the month and year of manufacture. 

9.1 AS/ Certification l\/larking — Optional, details available with the Indian Standards Institution.
